traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Aizoaceae with Molluginaceae, Tetragoniaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves alternate or opposite, sometimes whorled; leaves simple; veins single, pinnate or palmate; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes polygamous, rarely monoecious or dioecious; ovary superior, half inferior or inferior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary, in cymes or in heads, sometimes in racemes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, sometimes tepals; fruit capsule or berry, sometimes drupe or samara; stamens (1-) 5 to 120; carpels (1-) 2 to 5 (-20). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 371, 372, family Aizoaceae: leaf incision none; read as "none".

traits.flowering_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 371, 372, family Aizoaceae: flowering position both; read as "both".

traits.perianth.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add absent (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 371, 372: tepals (uniseriate calyx; corolla absent).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Aizoaceae (read 2026-10-16): alternate or opposite; the large mesemb subfamilies have opposite pairs (weighting inferred).

traits.fruit_type.note: DELTA Aizoaceae incl. the mesembs (read 2026-10-17; ~1,100 spp, 126 genera): fruit usually a capsule, fleshy only rarely (berry sometimes). Wikipedia Aizoaceae (read 2026-10-17; ~1,800 spp, 135 genera) adds that the capsules are often hygrochastic. Berries mainly Carpobrotus; nut-like or drupe-like fruits in Tetragonia.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Aizoaceae (read 2026-10-17): grouped flowers usually in cymes or heads, the ultimate units cymose, flowers otherwise single. Wikipedia Aizoaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers axillary, single or in few-flowered cymes. Both put cymes ahead; heads are only a minority state (Sesuvioideae and Aizooideae), so lowered to sometimes.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Wikipedia Aizoaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves opposite or alternate, and the family is dominated by the Ruschioideae radiation; DELTA (read 2026-10-17) lists alternate or opposite, with false whorls. Weighted by species (approximate, not read this session): Ruschioideae (~1,500 of ~1,800 spp; Ruschia, Delosperma, Lampranthus, Conophytum, Drosanthemum) have opposite, often basally joined leaves; alternate leaves are in Tetragonia, Aizoon, Galenia and part of Mesembryanthemum (~200).

traits.ovary_position.note: DELTA Aizoaceae (read 2026-10-17): ovary superior to inferior, no usual state. Our weighting by subfamily size (approximate, not read this session): the inferior ovary of Ruschioideae and Mesembryanthemoideae (~1,600 spp) outweighs the half-inferior ovaries of Aizooideae and Tetragonia and the superior ovary of Sesuvioideae (~200 together).
